## K16 · K16-churn-ceiling — sched-budget-churn's shell ceiling moves with every kernel speed change: the case or the netting

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 4

Evidence: Ruled by architect-8 (.wash/local/K16-churn-ceiling-ruling.md): the shell variant's upper bound on the victim is not a rule - R12 is a floor and the carving sections over-charge the carver by design, so the victim's share follows the kernel's speed; the bound becomes (500 - TOL, 1000) like the other variants, with one uncommitted evidence run (the entry-wait count put back into the lift must fail the oracle's lift check) and scheduling.md's Inheritance sentence and Responsiveness numbers rewritten, the '650 and 643' sentence deleted. Forwarded to K16's implementer; checked at K16's review. K21 needs no change of its own.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `4680e5dc10bb95c2a7e5a80cb7e8cdd9` · 2026-10-03T07:01:05Z

> K16's implementer (main 5f9f9d61c + commit 1, walks by live thread): rv64 sched-budget-churn's shell variant FAILS, victim net 569-581 against the 450-550 band on every seed, where main gives 501; bisect main 501 / commit 1 576 / 1+4 575 / WIP 2 573-581; rv32 passes; on the K20 base it passed, so it is commit 1 with INIT1 under it. Commit 1 only makes walks cheaper: the shell's audits fall 726 -> 661 ms of a ~2 s window while the victim's gross rises 319 -> 386, i.e. ~65 ms freed by audits plus ~70 ms off the shell side all land on the victim. The implementer reads it as kernel time on the shell's slice that the oracle does not net out (scheduling.md's audit-billed run gave 650), and a cheaper audit moving where slices end. This is the fourth package to meet this case's ceiling from a different side (K18 share-vs-window, B5 the net judge, K20 timer billing, K21 the ring). A ceiling that fails when the kernel gets faster is measuring the kernel's speed, not a scheduling rule. Please rule: is the shell variant's upper bound a rule at all (what property does 'the victim gets at most 550' guard - the floor guards the victim, the ceiling guards the shell's share, which K18's netting says should be judged net of the checked build's work), and if it is, what the oracle must net so the bound holds across kernel speeds; else the ceiling goes or becomes a recorded number. Logs: .worktrees/k16/.k16/churn-{main,c1,c14,wip}.txt. K16 proceeds on commits 2-3 meanwhile; K21's rebased bench is running on the same base and may show it too.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `4641e9a0ee1eb3efe6e70831fda7cb05` · 2026-10-03T07:05:51Z

> The shell variant's ceiling on the victim is not a rule, so it goes. Full ruling and exact lines: .wash/local/K16-churn-ceiling-ruling.md.
> 
> Why: R12 is a floor ("at least its weight's share"). The carving sections over-charge the carver on purpose. A budget running while carved accrues its lead at the weight it kept, "over-charged, never ahead" (scheduling.md, "Running while carved down" and "The lead follows the weight"), and the program's own comment says the shell's create and destroy calls count at its halved weight. So the victim gets half, plus the shell's carved-down time at double price, and that amount follows the kernel's speed: 501 on main and 576 at commit 1 are both what the rules give. What the ceiling was put there for (creating and destroying a never-run child moves nothing; the entry-wait double count) is exact arithmetic. It is judged exactly by the oracle's recomputed lifts, weight changes and rank-order picks, by mutation R12LiftCountsEntryWait and by the stride host test. Audit netting stays guarded by the gate's audit-billed negative run.
> 
> K16 does three things:
> 1. The shell variant's bounds become (500-TOL, 1000), like the other variants. Rewrite the program's comments.
> 2. One evidence run, uncommitted: put the entry-wait count back into the lift locally and run rv64 sched-budget-churn. The oracle's lift check must fail; report that line. If it passes, stop and ask me.
> 3. scheduling.md's Inheritance sentence and the Responsiveness numbers, as written in the file; delete the "650 and 643" sentence. testbench.md is unchanged.
> 
> This is not an owner choice. K21's bench, if it shows the same failure, is covered by the same ruling once K16 lands; it needs no change of its own.
